summary: Assess Basel III final reforms across credit, operational, and market risk. Build practical capital and reporting outputs. Explore the course.
lede: Basel III final reforms revise how banks assess credit, operational and market risk and translate these into risk-weighted assets and capital needs. This course is for bank risk, finance, treasury, audit and supervisory professionals who need to assess implementation impacts and support capital and reporting decisions. Participants compare standardized and internal-ratings-based credit approaches, assess the output floor, SMA and FRTB, and map data lineage, validation controls and reporting reconciliation into an implementation plan.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who interpret prudential capital requirements or translate them into bank models, reporting data, controls, and management decisions. It suits intermediate practitioners with working familiarity with banking risk or capital concepts. This course is designed for: Banking supervisors assessing Basel capital implementation evidence and prudential reporting. Prudential regulators reviewing banks’ output-floor calculations and reform transition plans. Bank credit-risk analysts mapping revised exposure classes and risk weights. Operational-risk specialists assessing SMA inputs, loss data, and control evidence. Market-risk analysts evaluating FRTB reporting and trading-book capital impacts. Bank CROs overseeing capital adequacy, risk appetite, and implementation governance. Bank capital-planning analysts forecasting risk-weighted assets and capital requirements. Treasury professionals incorporating Basel capital impacts into funding and balance-sheet decisions. Bank finance managers reconciling regulatory capital figures with reporting data. Banking auditors and consultants testing reform controls and implementation readiness.
modules: IRB Credit Risk and Output Floor
prerequisites: Working familiarity with bank risk, finance, treasury, capital adequacy, or prudential reporting is recommended. No coding is required. Advanced model and regulatory interpretation topics are taught at operational application level, not technical-engineering level.
